title: Lifting split-torus homomorphisms over a complete Noetherian local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $k=R/\mathfrak m$, and suppose that the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R/\mathfrak m^n$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme means an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over $S$. Let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For $r\geq0$ set $T=\operatorname{Spec}R[x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_r,y_r]/(x_iy_i-1)_{1\leq i\leq r}$, with $\Delta(x_i)=x_i\otimes x_i$, $\Delta(y_i)=y_i\otimes y_i$, counit $x_i,y_i\mapsto1$, and inverse interchanging $x_i$ and $y_i$; for $r=0$ this is the trivial $S$-group. Every homomorphism of $k$-group schemes $f_0:T_k\to G_k$ lifts to a homomorphism of $S$-group schemes $f:T\to G$ whose special fibre is exactly $f_0$. If $f_0$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], then every such lift $f$ is a closed immersion. Neither algebraic closedness of $k$ nor reductivity or connectedness of $G$ is assumed.

source.place: WANTED locally; Brian Conrad, Reductive group schemes (2014), Corollary B.3.5, printed pp.292-293, restricted to H = G_m^r. Its direct proof uses Theorem B.3.2, Corollary B.2.6 and Remark B.2.4. Read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf, PDF pages 292-293.

proof.text: For any $R$-algebra $A$, the maps sending $x_i$ to $e_{v_i}$ and $y_i$ to $e_{-v_i}$ identify the displayed torus algebra after scalar extension with $A[\mathbf Z^r]$, where $v_i$ is the $i$th standard basis vector. The inverse sends $e_{(n_i)}$ to $\prod_i x_i^{\max(n_i,0)}y_i^{\max(-n_i,0)}$. Multiplication and the three Hopf operations agree on these generators. The affine fibre-product formula identifies scalar extension with tensoring; the coefficient maps $R[\mathbf Z^r]\otimes_RA\leftrightarrows A[\mathbf Z^r]$, $e_v\otimes a\leftrightarrow ae_v$, are inverse. Thus $T_A=D_A(\mathbf Z^r)$ compatibly with all quotient maps. The displayed finite presentation also proves that $T$ is locally of finite presentation. It is formally smooth directly: a unit $a_0$ modulo a square-zero ideal lifts to a unit $a$, since a lift $b$ of its inverse has $ab=1+c$ with $c^2=0$, and $b(1-c)$ is an inverse of $a$. Apply this independently to each of the $r$ units. Thus $T$ is smooth by the smoothness definition. Put $R_n=R/\mathfrak m^n$ for $n\geq1$. The kernel $J_n=\mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ of $R_{n+1}\to R_n$ is square-zero since $2n\geq n+1$.

source.place: Corollary B.3.5, printed p.292, successive quotient rings; explicit split-source coordinate identifications.

proof.text: Set $u_1=f_0$ over $R_1=k$. Suppose $u_n:T_{R_n}\to G_{R_n}$ has been chosen. Smooth base-change stability makes $G_{R_{n+1}}$ smooth over $R_{n+1}$, and the affine fibre-product formula makes it affine. Apply the square-zero lifting lemma over $A=R_{n+1}$, with ideal $J_n$ and finitely generated group $M=\mathbf Z^r$. Step 1 identifies the source and reduction with its $D_A(M)$ and $D_{A/J_n}(M)$. It gives $u_{n+1}$ reducing exactly to $u_n$, as a group homomorphism. Recursive choice gives a compatible family $(u_n)_{n\geq1}$ with first term the prescribed $f_0$.

source.place: Corollary B.3.5, printed p.292, infinitesimal existence step.

proof.text: Apply effectivity of formal diagonalizable-source homomorphisms with $A=R$, $M=\mathbf Z^r$, and this family. The ring is Noetherian, local and complete by hypothesis, the source is split by Step 1, and the target is affine of finite type: $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is locally of finite presentation over $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, so by the affine-opens criterion for local finite presentation, applied with $U=G$ and $V=S$, the coordinate map $R\to B$ is of finite presentation, and in particular $B$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra. Effectivity produces an $R$-group homomorphism $f:T\to G$ with reductions $u_n$. At $n=1$ this is exactly $f_0$, proving existence.

source.place: Corollary B.3.5, printed p.292, algebraization via Theorem B.3.2(1).

proof.text: Now let $f$ be any lift and suppose $f_0$ is a closed immersion. Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $L=R[\mathbf Z^r]$, let $f^*:B\to L$ be its coordinate map and $\epsilon:B\to R$ its identity section. The affine fibre-product formula gives $K=T\times_{G,e}S=\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_{B,\epsilon}R)$. This tensor algebra is $L/I$, where $I=(f^*(b)-\epsilon(b):b\in B)$: its universal property is precisely equality of these two images of $B$. Hence $K\to T$ is a closed immersion by the affine quotient criterion. Its points over any $S$-scheme $X$ are the $t\in T(X)$ with $f(t)=1$; multiplication and inverse preserve this condition, so their restrictions give the subgroup operations. Reducing the quotient presentation to $k$ identifies $K_k$ with $\ker f_0$. The coordinate map of $f_0$ is surjective by the closed-immersion criterion. Two maps from its target coordinate algebra that agree on its source therefore agree everywhere, so $f_0$ is injective on points over every affine $k$-scheme. In particular the kernel has only its identity element on every such test scheme; equivalently its affine representing algebra is $k$. Thus $K_k=1_k$ as a group scheme.

source.place: Corollary B.3.5, printed pp.292-293, reduction to the scheme-theoretic kernel; elementary affine presentation written out.

proof.text: Apply the local split-torus closed-subgroup lemma to $K\hookrightarrow T$. The base ring is Noetherian local and Step 4 verifies its exact scheme-theoretic special-fibre hypothesis; flatness of $K$ is not needed. It gives $K=1_S$. For every $S$-scheme $X$, if $f(t)=f(t\prime)$, then $t(t\prime)^{-1}\in K(X)=\{1\}$, so $t=t\prime$. Thus $f$ is a monomorphism in the precise functor-of-points sense required by the relative torus monomorphism lemma. The latter applies: $T$ is the displayed split torus, $G$ is of finite presentation by hypothesis and is separated over $S$ by the affine-source separatedness lemma. It follows that $f$ is a closed immersion. This argument applied to an arbitrary lift, not just the lift constructed above. All formulas and arguments allow $r=0$.

source.place: Corollary B.3.5, printed pp.292-293, kernel criterion; kernel triviality via Exercise 2.4.3(iii), printed p.76, and closedness via the existing torus-monomorphism node.

proof_origin.place: Conrad Corollary B.3.5, printed pp.292-293, with the split-source form of Theorem B.3.2(1), the square-zero consequence of Corollary B.2.6 and Remark B.2.4, and the torsion kernel argument of Exercise 2.4.3(iii). Local archive unavailable; elementary coordinate elaborations and assembly supplied by NZ.

The Conrad source PDF is not in literature/, so I checked each new node by proving it myself. (1) square-zero-diagonalizable-hom-lift: true. The morphism lifts by formal smoothness, and the obstruction to a homomorphism lift is Hochschild H^2 with Lie(G)⊗J coefficients, which vanishes for diagonalizable groups over any base (torsion M included). (2) adic-diagonalizable-hom-effectivity: true. For b in B, write φ̂(b)=Σc_m e_m. Comparing coefficients of Δb gives Σ_i x_{i,m} y_{i,m'} = δ_{mm'} c_m. The rows r_m generate a finitely generated submodule of A^N (A Noetherian), so c_m≠0 for only finitely many m and φ̂(B) lies in A[M]. (3) local-torus-subgroup-special-trivial: true without flatness. K[n] is finite over A, so it is trivial by Nakayama; each fibre is diagonalizable with trivial torsion, hence trivial; then Q_q=pQ_q and Nakayama give Q=0.
